newsitem.title: USA: U.S. July jobs strong but slightly overstated - BLS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. July jobs strong but slightly overstated - BLS.

text.p: The July employment picture was strong but slightly overstated, a Bureau of Labor Statistics official said Friday.
BLS economist Harvey Hamel told Reuters Financial Television that 48,000 of the 316,000 increase in non-farm payrolls represented seasonal adjustment for jobs in local government education.
"There's no question that employment is strong...the 316,000 I think it may be just a bit overstated because of the education component," he said.

Hamel said seasonal adjustment in this area was very difficult in the summer due to changing dates of school closings and some shift to year-round teacher contracts and even some year-round schooling.
Prior to adjustment there were probably 1.2 million people expected to leave school payrolls between June and July.
"So if u miss that by 30,000 or 40,000 it's not a big piece of the 1.2 million but it impacts on employment for the month," he said.
